nodes.label: C Closures and Upvalues
nodes.rationale: Binds upvalues to C functions via lua_pushcclosure and lua_upvalueindex; zero upvalues yields a light C function pointer with no memory allocation

nodes.label: Lua C Registry
nodes.rationale: Predefined table at LUA_REGISTRYINDEX storing C-side persistent Lua values, LUA_RIDX_MAINTHREAD, LUA_RIDX_GLOBALS, and integer references via luaL_ref

nodes.label: Chunks and Binary Precompilation
nodes.rationale: Compilation unit treated as an anonymous variadic function with _ENV upvalue; precompiled binary chunks load via the same interface as source text but are not verified against malicious corruption

nodes.label: Coroutines (Collaborative Multithreading)
nodes.rationale: Independent execution threads that suspend only via explicit yield, supporting collaborative multithreading on platforms without OS threads

nodes.label: C Debug Interface (lua_Debug and lua_Hook)
nodes.rationale: Replaces built-in debugging with an introspection and hook API (call, return, tail call, line, count) for external debuggers and profilers

nodes.label: Environments (_ENV and _G)
nodes.rationale: Translates global variable references var to _ENV.var inside an implicit _ENV upvalue per chunk, enabling isolated chunk environments without altering the global environment stored in the C registry

nodes.label: Automatic Garbage Collection (Incremental and Generational)
nodes.rationale: Collects dead objects automatically in incremental mark-and-sweep or generational minor/major modes; keeps registry-reachable objects alive because Lua cannot inspect C pointers

nodes.label: Global Variable Declarations (Lua 5.5)
nodes.rationale: Chunks start with implicit 'global *', which is voided inside explicit global declarations so programs can enforce declared-only or read-only (global<const> *) global access

nodes.label: Lua Eight Basic Types
nodes.rationale: Dynamic typing where values carry their own type (nil, boolean, number, string, function, userdata, thread, table) and all values are first-class

nodes.label: Lua 5.5 Language
nodes.rationale: Lightweight embeddable scripting language written in clean C using a register-based virtual machine and associative arrays to support procedural, OOP, functional, and data-driven programming

nodes.label: Package and Module System (require / package)
nodes.rationale: Configurable module resolution via package.searchers (preload, Lua path, C path, all-in-one loader) with caching in registry-backed package.loaded

nodes.label: String Library, Patterns, and Binary Pack/Unpack
nodes.norm_label: string library, patterns, and binary pack/unpack

nodes.label: Lua Table (Associative Array)
nodes.rationale: Sole data-structuring mechanism representing arrays, records, sets, and objects; converts integral float keys to integers to avoid key ambiguity and defines sequences via single borders for O(log n) length

nodes.label: Userdata (Full and Light)
nodes.rationale: Stores arbitrary C data or pointers in Lua variables while prohibiting creation or modification in Lua code to guarantee host data integrity

nodes.label: Lua Auxiliary Library (lauxlib.h)
nodes.rationale: Higher-level C API helpers (luaL_*) implemented strictly on top of the basic C API to standardize argument checking, buffers, references, and state initialization

nodes.label: Lua 5.5 Incompatibilities with Lua 5.4
nodes.rationale: Catalogs breaking language, library, and C API changes from 5.4 to 5.5 including 'global' keyword, read-only for-loop variables, 15-deep __call cap, 250-result cap, lua_newstate seed, and LUA_GCPARAM

nodes.label: Lua C API (lua.h)
nodes.rationale: Fully reentrant C interface with no global variables, storing all interpreter state dynamically inside lua_State

nodes.label: Lua Standard Libraries (lualib.h)
nodes.rationale: Separate C modules implemented through the official C API; host programs explicitly load or preload them via luaL_openlibs or luaL_openselectedlibs

nodes.label: Garbage-Collection Finalizers (__gc)
nodes.rationale: Transiently resurrects dead objects marked with __gc at setmetatable time so finalizers can release external resources in reverse marking order; errors in finalizers emit warnings rather than propagating

nodes.label: Lexical Scoping and Upvalues
nodes.rationale: Inner functions freely access enclosing local variables (upvalues), instantiating fresh closures per execution of a local declaration

nodes.label: Metatables and Metamethods
nodes.rationale: Allows customizable operator, indexing, call, and lifecycle behavior via ordinary tables keyed by '__event' names; tables and full userdata have per-instance metatables while other types share one per type

nodes.label: Number Subtypes (Integer and Float)
nodes.rationale: Unifies integers (with two's complement wrap-around) and IEEE 754 floats under a single number type with explicit subtype rules and automatic conversions, supporting 64-bit or 32-bit builds (LUA_32BITS)

nodes.label: Proper Tail Calls
nodes.rationale: Reuses the caller's stack frame for 'return f(args)' outside to-be-closed scopes, enabling unbounded recursion while trading off caller debug stack information

nodes.label: To-be-closed Variables (<close>)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic cleanup invoking __close metamethods in reverse declaration order on normal block exit, break/goto/return, or error

nodes.label: Lua Virtual Stack
nodes.rationale: Bridges C and Lua values with positive/negative indices and acceptable-index semantics to avoid redundant stack-top checks in C functions

nodes.label: Weak Tables and Ephemeron Tables
nodes.rationale: Configured via __mode ('k', 'v', 'kv') to let GC collect unreferenced keys/values; ephemeron tables (weak keys, strong values) break key-value reference cycles and retain weak keys of resurrected objects until after finalizers run

nodes.label: Two-Column Wide Glyph Overwrite Collision
nodes.rationale: NetHack assumes 1-column cells while PDCursesMod inserts DUMMY_CHAR_NEXT_TO_FULLWIDTH in the adjacent cell, which NetHack immediately overwrites.

nodes.label: unicode_val() 6-Hex-Digit Parsing Limit
nodes.rationale: src/utf8map.c:unicode_val() stops after 6 hex digits (dcount < 7), truncating U+0001F41C to U+01F4.

nodes.label: Windows WriteConsoleOutputW CHAR_INFO 16-bit WCHAR Limit
nodes.rationale: CHAR_INFO holds only one 16-bit WCHAR per cell, preventing UTF-16 surrogate pairs required for SMP emoji (>= U+10000).

nodes.label: pline Format Specifier & Logic Invariance Rule
nodes.norm_label: pline format specifier & logic invariance rule
nodes.rationale: Preserves specifier count, order, types, and argument expressions across pline/pline_dir/pline_xy/pline_mon/vpline to prevent crashes and control-flow drift.

nodes.label: Oracle Line UTF-8 <80-Byte Constraint
nodes.rationale: src/rumors.c reads oracle lines into line[COLNO] (80 bytes), so dat/oracles.txt and util/makedefs.c special_oracle[] lines must stay under 80 UTF-8 bytes.

nodes.label: Curses Window Port Adoption
nodes.rationale: Adopted community curses window-port (PDCurses on Windows, ncurses on macOS/Unix) for flexible multi-line status layouts and window management.

nodes.label: BL_RESET and BL_FLUSH Status Update Protocol
nodes.norm_label: bl_reset and bl_flush status update protocol
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes BL_RESET (full redraw of all status fields) from BL_FLUSH (commit buffered changes at end of bot()) to optimize tty and GUI status rendering.

nodes.label: isaac64 Separate Core and Display PRNG
nodes.norm_label: isaac64 separate core and display prng
nodes.rationale: Uses separate isaac64 PRNG contexts for core gameplay and display (e.g., hallucination) so display changes do not perturb gameplay RNG.

nodes.label: perm_invent Moved from flags to iflags
nodes.norm_label: perm_invent moved from flags to iflags
nodes.rationale: Keeps UI-only persistent inventory state out of save files while preserving save file compatibility.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive sortloot Option
nodes.rationale: Avoids reordering the underlying object list so reverting sortloot to none restores original order and full-pack identify does not skip items.

nodes.label: Centralized has_color() Color Availability Table
nodes.rationale: Replaces per-port string checks during map cell updates with one table-driven check in src/windows.c.

nodes.label: S_hero_override and Pet Override Symbols
nodes.rationale: Added per request from a blind player to give pets and the player unique overriding map symbols.

nodes.label: Status Highlight Color & Empty Data File Crash Fixes
nodes.norm_label: status highlight color & empty data file crash fixes

nodes.label: Sequential makedefs -s Data File Build
nodes.rationale: makedefs -s generates engrave, epitaph, and bogusmon simultaneously; running parallel make instances stomped on each other's outputs.

nodes.label: MDGREP Conditional Filtering
nodes.rationale: Allows master documentation and dungeon.def files to embed platform- and config-conditional lines using ^?, ^!, ^:, ^. control lines.

nodes.label: include/optlist.h Option Macro System
nodes.rationale: Expands NHOPTB/NHOPTC/NHOPTP/NHOPTO macros across NHOPT_PROTO, NHOPT_ENUM, and NHOPT_PARSE phases to keep prototypes, enums, and allopt[] synchronized.

nodes.label: struct sound_procs and Sound Triggers
nodes.rationale: Decouples NetHack core audio events from platform sound libraries and supports multiple soundlibs in one binary via a function-pointer table and trigger bitmask.

nodes.label: struct window_procs Interface Specification
nodes.rationale: Separates core game logic from UI rendering across tty, X11, curses, Windows, and custom ports using a uniform window_procs table.

nodes.label: NetHack Core Window Types (NHW_* and WIN_*)
nodes.norm_label: nethack core window types (nhw_* and win_*)

nodes.label: pline and Option Buffer Overflow Hardening
nodes.norm_label: pline and option buffer overflow hardening
nodes.rationale: Hardened pline(), raw_printf(), config_error_add(), choose_windows(), add_menu_coloring(), and sym_val() against buffer overflows and switched pline.c to vsnprintf.

nodes.label: Ascension Achievements
nodes.rationale: Grouped with conduct during end-of-game disclosure to limit the number of disclosure prompts while recording progress toward ultimate ascension.

nodes.label: Beatitude (Blessed, Uncursed, Cursed / BUC)
nodes.rationale: Uses the designation 'uncursed' rather than 'unblessed' and omits redundant 'uncursed' text by default via implicit_uncursed when deduceable from other attributes.

nodes.label: Character Races
nodes.rationale: Separated race from profession starting in NetHack 3.3 (removing the Elf class in favor of an Elf race and adding Dwarf, Gnome, and Orc alongside Human) to expand role/race combinations.

nodes.label: Command and Keybinding System
nodes.rationale: Extended '#' commands and meta-key shortcuts were introduced because single-character commands exhausted the available alphabet.

nodes.label: Voluntary Conduct Challenges
nodes.rationale: Tracks optional self-imposed restrictions (dietary, atheist, pacifist, illiterate, weaponless, wishless, Sokoban, etc.) for extra bragging rights without requiring them for a normal win.

nodes.label: Display Options, Map Symbols, and Tiles
nodes.norm_label: display options, map symbols, and tiles
nodes.rationale: Display modes (monochrome ASCII, color ASCII, graphical tiles, UTF-8 Unicode glyphs) have no gameplay differences; default ASCII symbols are used in the Guidebook because they are common to all ports.

nodes.label: Explore Mode and Debug (Wizard) Mode
nodes.rationale: Explore mode lets novices keep save files and cheat death in exchange for exclusion from the high score list; debug mode exists to diagnose program bugs rather than provide god-like powers.

nodes.label: Pattern-Based Message Types, Menu Colors, and User Sounds
nodes.norm_label: pattern-based message types, menu colors, and user sounds
nodes.rationale: Uses POSIX extended regular expressions (or glob fallback) evaluated sequentially where later rules override earlier rules so exceptions can follow general rules.

nodes.label: NetHack 5.0.1
nodes.rationale: Modernized to comply with the C99 standard and moved to Lua-based level/dungeon generation and quest texts in 5.0.0; chosen as version 5.0 over 4.0 to avoid ambiguity with existing community variants.

nodes.label: NetHack Version Evolution (1.4 to 5.0.1)
nodes.rationale: Retired version numbers 3.4.4, 3.5, and 3.5.0 after a leaked 2014 WIP snapshot, shifted to public GitHub/SourceForge development for 3.7 WIP, and released as 5.0.0 rather than 4.0 to avoid confusion with variants.

nodes.label: Player Attributes and Status Lines
nodes.rationale: statuslines:2 is the default because a basic 24-line terminal is not tall enough for a third status line, even though two lines can truncate when multiple conditions are present.

nodes.label: Rogue Level
nodes.rationale: Designed as a deliberate tribute to Hack's ancestor game Rogue, altering display symbols (* for gold, % for stairs), room lighting behavior, doorless doorways, and monster generation.

nodes.label: Scoring System
nodes.rationale: Quitting preserves 100% of carried gold whereas dying recovers only 90% due to finder's fees, creating a strategic risk/reward decision.

nodes.label: Sokoban Dungeon Branch
nodes.rationale: Because NetHack does not support an undo capability, Sokoban levels include at least one extra boulder and permit rule-breaking workarounds (squeezing past or destroying/creating boulders) at the cost of a silent luck penalty tracked as a conduct.

nodes.label: Weapon and Spell Proficiency (#enhance)
nodes.rationale: Weapon and spell skill slots share a capped total pool, so skills do not advance automatically upon reaching training thresholds; the player must actively allocate them via #enhance.

nodes.label: AD&D and Unearthed Arcana Rules Influence
nodes.norm_label: ad&d and unearthed arcana rules influence

nodes.label: Configuration System (.nethackrc, NETHACKOPTIONS, sysconf)
nodes.rationale: Centralizes user options, conditional CHOOSE profiles, and sysconf admin controls (such as DUMPLOGFILE, LIVELOG, and SYSCF). LIVELOG is left disabled on single-player installs to avoid unbounded log growth, and autopickup defaulted to off starting in 5.0.0.

nodes.label: Accessibility Configuration for Blind Players
nodes.rationale: Enables play via Braille readers and speech synthesizers using standard ASCII (symset:plain), traditional menus, NETHACK_MSGHANDLER external message routing, relative compass coordinates, and directional/monster-spotting messages.

nodes.label: Level Persistence and Monster Stasis
nodes.rationale: Leaving a dungeon level deactivates and stores it on disk, placing monsters on unvisited/inactive levels into stasis while reactivating previously visited levels upon return.

nodes.label: Object Filtering (Class, Shop, BUCX, Novelty)
nodes.rationale: Combines OR within each filter category (class, unpaid status, BUCX beatitude, novelty) and AND across categories so players can batch-manipulate inventory precisely.

nodes.label: Shortest-Path Travel Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Computes a shortest path over known map squares (or guesses if no path is known) and implicitly forces the nopickup ('m') prefix while stopping on interesting events like 'G'.

nodes.label: fetch.bat lua (Lua 5.4.8)
nodes.rationale: NetHack 5.0 for Windows requires 3rd party Lua 5.4.8 source not bundled in the NetHack distribution or repository.

nodes.label: fetch.cmd pdcursesmod
nodes.rationale: Optional 3rd party pdcursesmod source is fetched into lib/ only if curses interface support is desired.

nodes.label: sys/windows/Makefile.nmake
nodes.rationale: Default Makefile targets 32-bit x86 so compiled binaries run on the largest number of existing Windows environments.

nodes.label: Windows Build Helper Tools (makedefs, tilemap, tile2bmp, uudecode, dlb)
nodes.norm_label: windows build helper tools (makedefs, tilemap, tile2bmp, uudecode, dlb)

nodes.label: 32-bit vs 64-bit Save and Bones Incompatibility
nodes.rationale: In NetHack 5.0.1, nethack.exe and nethackw.exe of the same architecture share datafiles, save files, and bones files, but save and bones files are not interchangeable between 32-bit x86 and 64-bit x64 builds or different platforms.

nodes.rationale: Cross-compiling between x64 and ARM64 requires completing a native host build first so host-native uudecode.exe, makedefs.exe, tilemap.exe, tile2bmp.exe, and dlb.exe are available during subsequent build steps.

nodes.label: Centaur Tiles (Tiles 264-269)
nodes.rationale: Centaur tiles (plains, forest, mountain) have no gender differentiation because the different types of centaurs are already extremely difficult to tell apart.

nodes.label: Dwarf (Tiles 92-93)
nodes.rationale: Male and female dwarfs are not differentiated in any way, following the Terry Pratchett tradition in Unseen Academicals that it is nearly impossible to tell a dwarf's gender.

nodes.label: Genetic Engineer (Tiles 432-433)
nodes.rationale: Male and female genetic engineers look identical because the existing genetic engineer tile is considered perfect.

nodes.label: Giant Ant (Tiles 0-1)
nodes.rationale: Female ants are slightly larger than male ants as in real life; wings were omitted on male ants because doing so would lead to confusion.

nodes.label: Ixoth (Tiles 742-743)
nodes.rationale: Ixoth is a male red dragon; his tile was corrected because for many years it erroneously depicted a demon.

nodes.label: Wolf (Tiles 40-41)
nodes.rationale: Female wolves have slightly shorter tails because making them smaller would make winter wolves look very similar to winter wolf cubs.

nodes.label: Clean-Shaven Female Humanoid Shorthand

nodes.label: Female Clothing, Crown & Hairstyle Variants

nodes.label: Gender Differentiation in Monster Tiles

nodes.label: C99 Modernization and Legacy Macro Removal
nodes.norm_label: c99 modernization and legacy macro removal
nodes.rationale: Modernizes codebase from K&R C to C99, removing obsolete STATIC_DCL/OVL/VAR/PTR, register keywords, and pre-ANSI #if LINT hacks.

nodes.label: Outdated Platform Code Relocation
nodes.rationale: Moves unmaintained platform code (Amiga, Atari, BeOS, classic Mac, OS/2, WinCE, Qt3, GEM, GNOME) into outdated/ and drops SYSFLAGS and MFLOPPY conditional code.

nodes.label: Options Overhaul (optlist.h / allopt[])
nodes.rationale: Moves option definitions into include/optlist.h, unifies boolean and compound options into allopt[], gives each option dedicated set/get/post-selection handlers, and adds doc/options.txt.

nodes.label: Gender-Neutral Fellow (%s) Callout Revision
nodes.rationale: Changed %s in src/questpgr.c to gender-neutral 同胞 while keeping %S as 息子／娘 and rewriting literal family/adversary contexts to 家族 or 若造.

nodes.label: Quest Pronoun, Fellow, and Perception Macro Rules
nodes.norm_label: quest pronoun, fellow, and perception macro rules
nodes.rationale: Placeholder macros (%nh/%ni/%nj, %s/%S/%sp, %x) carry embedded Japanese particles or blind-aware verbs, so sentences must be restructured without duplicating particles or altering placeholder counts and order.

nodes.label: Natural Japanese Translation Quality Standard
